item.title: New Approaches to Address the Role of Gold in Sudan’s Civil War
item.description: Revenues from gold are a key driver of the conflict in Sudan. Recent EU sanctions are a start, but much more needs to be done to ensure the gold trade no longer finances bloodshed in the world’s most abandoned humanitarian crisis.

item.title: Proving Ground: China’s Strategic Ratcheting of the Philippines and the Indo-Pacific’s Gray Zone Problem
item.description: China’s maritime gray zone operations in the West Philippine Sea are the “tip of the spear” for China’s pressure campaign against the Philippines. It is essential that policymakers do not lose sight of the rest of the spear.

item.title: What Happens if Congress Codifies Russia Sanctions?
item.description: The Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 would codify roughly 6,800 designations and create a new tariff authority aimed at the largest buyers of Russian energy. Whether it produces real pressure on Moscow depends on executive branch implementation.

item.title: Section 301 Tariffs and China: A Risky Gambit
item.description: Scott Kennedy and Claire Reade outline how USTR’s new Section 301 tariffs face legal hurdles, have not achieved their intended economic results, and are making it more difficult for the United States and allies to align in tackling China’s non-market practices.

item.title: Brussels vs. Brussels: The EU’s Data Act and the DMA’s Clash Over Cloud
item.description: The European Union preliminarily designated AWS and Azure as gatekeepers under the Digital Markets Act. Both already fall under the Data Act, and the overlapping rules risk undermining Europe's cloud sector while deepening its reliance on U.S. providers.

item.title: Beyond Tracing: Anticipatory Technical Exploitation and Smart Friction
item.description: Tracing how adversaries acquired yesterday’s technology should be the beginning, not the end, of technical exploitation. Anticipatory analysis can reveal likely substitutions and help policymakers shape adaptation through targeted smart friction.

item.title: Old Friends, New Calculations: A Reset in China-North Korea Relations
item.description: China’s shift toward deeper ties with North Korea, including within military affairs, brings important implications worth exploring.
